defect: PLAN §9's tollgate fixture: an Improve-phase exit call where T-19 (Pilot Plan) was never saved to the project at all -- 'pilot skipped' -- while the one artifact that IS saved, T-20 (Proof), narrates a full rollout in its free-text `notes`: 'We rolled this out to the full team immediately -- no need for a small pilot first, this is now our standard way of working across every shift.' The proof itself is clean (stable before/after, no confound, threshold met) so the ONLY defect under test is the missing-pilot / premature-full-implementation pattern, not a shaky proof.

gate_improve_to_control.reason: not-yet-built: Improve gates (proof/remaining-gap) ship in M4.

deterministic_layer.notes: Confirmed live against a real scratch project carrying only this T-20 (no T-01/T-03/T-15/T-18/T-19 saved at all): POST /gates/check {gate_id: improve_to_control} returns status=NOT_YET_BUILT -- gates.py's GATE_TABLE row for improve_to_control is still kind='stub' (gates.py source, not just its comment), so this gate does not block a phase-exit tollgate call on a missing pilot regardless of project state; it is not wired to require T-19's presence the way define_to_measure is wired to require T-03/T-04/T-05. Separately, advisor/modes.py's tollgate context selector loops over PHASE_TOOL_IDS['Improve'] = (T-18, T-19, T-20) and silently `continue`s past any tool_id with no saved artifact (context.py's own prescore loop) -- so a missing T-19 produces no explicit 'pilot missing' line anywhere in the tollgate call's deterministic context either, only fewer prescore entries than a fully-populated phase would have. Nothing in code stops, or even names, a premature Improve exit here -- only the advisor's own reading of the phase's actual tool coverage plus the T-20 narrative can catch it.

schema_note: Nothing schema-legal is blocked. ProofArtifact.pilot_ref is an unchecked, echoed-by-ref string (proof.py's own module docstring: 'echoed... never independently re-fetched' -- the same soft-cross-reference contract every *_ref field in this engine uses), so a T-20 can validate and save with a pilot_ref that does not correspond to any T-19 artifact ever actually saved in the project. This is in fact the realistic shape of the defect: someone typed a pilot reference without ever running (or saving) the pilot.
